title: Prime Day Is Here—These Are the Deals Worth Buying
gist: WIRED's master October 2026 Prime Day (Big Deal Days) roundup spans hundreds of tested products, but its signal is in the asides: broad 2026 price hikes by Apple, Amazon (Kindle/Echo in late August) and Microsoft mean many 'deals' merely restore 2025 prices, while the Mac Mini has been sold out most of the year due to demand for local agentic-AI machines.

themes.theme: Agentic AI pulls on Mac Mini supply

insights.claim: The Mac Mini has been sold out for most of 2026 because of surging interest in using it as a local machine for agentic AI, and the new M6 model is both faster and more expensive than ever.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Local agent workloads are creating real consumer-hardware demand for Apple silicon desktops — a tangible on-device AI tailwind for Apple.
insights.quote: The Mac Mini has been sold out for the majority of this year due to the rapid escalation of interest in using them as local, agentic AI machines.
insights.locator: The Mac Mini has been sold out

insights.claim: Amazon raised prices on Kindle and Echo devices at the end of August 2026 — e.g. Kindle Colorsoft base model from $250 to $290, Echo Show 11 by $30, Echo Show 8 to $200 — so Prime Day discounts are partly offsetting fresh hikes.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Even Amazon's subsidized first-party hardware is being repriced upward, indicating component/cost pressure that Amazon chose not to absorb.
insights.quote: While it was also hit with a price hike at the end of August, with the base model rising to $290 from $250, you can get it for $100 off during Amazon's sale.
insights.locator: While almost all of Amazon's Kindles

insights.claim: The Echo Studio (2nd Gen) was the only new Echo that did not get a price increase, which the reviewer uses as the test for whether a sale is genuine rather than 'a trick of the numbers'.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Evaluating discounts against pre-hike baselines is necessary in 2026; nominal percent-off figures overstate consumer savings.
insights.quote: But it's also the only new Echo that didn't get a price increase, so this sale isn't just a trick of the numbers.
insights.locator: The Echo Studio has been our favorite

insights.claim: Because Amazon raised Paperwhite and other Kindle prices, this Prime Day's Paperwhite discount is the worst WIRED has seen and the reviewer does not expect lower prices again.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Signals a durable reset in e-reader pricing and less aggressive promotional depth from Amazon devices.
insights.quote: since Amazon raised prices for the Paperwhite (among other Kindle models), I don't expect to see a lower price in the future anymore
insights.locator: If you're getting a new Kindle

insights.claim: Apple's price hikes earlier in 2026 eliminated most iPad deals; the 11-inch A16 iPad at $399 on Amazon is described as one of the only iPad deals that survived.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Apple appears to be tightening promotional channels alongside list-price increases, protecting margins.
insights.quote: The 11-inch iPad on Amazon is one of the only iPad deals that survived Apple’s price hikes earlier this year.
insights.locator: Despite all of Apple’s attempts to expand

insights.claim: Microsoft's Surface Laptop 13.8-inch also saw price increases in 2026, with sale events only bringing it back near 2025 levels, and the newer Snapdragon X2 model is judged poor value for a marginal performance step.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Price inflation is industry-wide in PCs, and next-gen Arm Windows silicon is not yet justifying its premium to reviewers.
insights.quote: My love for this laptop, which is both beautiful and full of useful features, has been deterred by its price increases this year.

insights.claim: The Asus Zenbook A14 is one of the few laptops whose price has steadily dropped over the past six months while all other laptop prices keep rising.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Outlier price declines may flag weak demand for first-gen Snapdragon X Windows laptops relative to inflating peers.
insights.quote: This is one of the few laptops that have steadily dropped in price over the past six months while all other prices keep rising.
insights.locator: This is one of the few laptops

insights.claim: Samsung's Galaxy S26 base model now ships with 256 GB of storage, and the reviewer is unsure when it will dip in price again given prices rising across the market.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Smartphone pricing is also caught in the 2026 upward drift, limiting promotional depth into the holidays.
insights.quote: This has been cheaper, but with prices on the rise across the market, I’m not sure when it will dip again.
insights.locator: If you want an Android phone

insights.claim: The MacBook Neo, called possibly the most controversial laptop of the year, ships with 8 GB of memory and an iPhone chip, while a MacBook Air with double the storage and RAM frequently sold for only $50 more in 2025.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Apple is segmenting downward with a phone-chip Mac; in an inflationary pricing year, the value gap vs. the Air is narrowing in Apple's favor on margins.
insights.quote: you might not notice the 8 GB of memory and iPhone chip inside and just enjoy the lower price
insights.locator: It might be the most controversial laptop

insights.claim: The M5 MacBook Air's price has gone up considerably over the past year, as with many of the best laptops, and the $1,099 Prime Day price is its lowest since June.
insights.speaker: Luke Larsen
insights.so_what: Corroborates a broad laptop ASP increase through 2026.
insights.quote: The price has gone up considerably over the past year, but that’s true of many of the best laptops.
insights.locator: I still find myself recommending the MacBook Air M5

insights.claim: WIRED says it tracks prices with several tools to avoid fake discounts and only includes products its team has personally tested, framing inflated reference prices as a known Prime Day hazard.
insights.speaker: Louryn Strampe
insights.so_what: Fake 'was' prices remain endemic on Amazon events; curated price-history sourcing is the defense.
insights.quote: We track prices using several tools to avoid falling for fake discounts.

insights.claim: Many smart-home gadgets in the roundup gate core features behind subscriptions — e.g. Birdfy's AI bird ID is limited to 20 uses/month without a $54/year plan and free storage is capped at three days, and Arlo cameras need $10–$20/month for subject recognition and cloud storage.
insights.speaker: Kat Merck
insights.so_what: Hardware vendors increasingly monetize via AI-feature subscriptions, making 'subscription-free' a selling point (e.g. Asus mesh Wi-Fi).
insights.quote: Without the $54/year subscription, you'll get 20 uses of AI ID per month, but be forewarned this feature isn’t great
